sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Greece, New York?
sections.html:
Greece is the largest town in Monroe County by population and sits directly northwest of Rochester, so a seller here competes with a deep supply of suburban houses. It was established on March 22, 1822, and it reaches from Ridge Road in the south to the Lake Ontario shoreline in the north.

The Rochester suburb is bordered by the city on the east, the town of Gates on the south, and the towns of Parma and Ogden on the west. According to Wikipedia's article on Greece, the town covers about 51 square miles, roughly 47.5 of them land. Wetlands and ponds, including Braddock Bay, line the northern edge near the lake. The disclosure form asks about wetlands and flood zones, so answer those lines from the lake side of town with care.

Ridge Road, which is NY-104, follows an old glacial lakeshore and carries most of the shopping. NY-18 (Latta Road) runs through North Greece, the Lake Ontario State Parkway crosses the northern part of town, and I-390 runs north and south through the east side. The same article records the town growing from about 25,500 people in 1950 to about 75,100 in 1970, and it notes that thousands of residents drove the Ridge to Kodak jobs in the 1940s.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Greece homes?
sections.html:
Greece housing is among the more affordable in the Rochester area, with a median owner-occupied value around $190,000. The table uses the Census Bureau's current town profile.

The estimate shows the town about 2.3 percent below its 2020 base, which means sellers are not riding a population surge. The average commute is about 20 minutes, a figure worth quoting to out-of-town buyers.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Greece and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Three districts serve the town: Greece Central, Hilton Central and Spencerport Central. Greece Central is by far the largest, with roughly 11,000 students, and it is the seventh largest district in New York State outside New York City. Its secondary schools are Arcadia, Athena, Olympia and Odyssey, with the Phoenix Academy for grades 7 to 12.

Put the district name in your listing or your message to a cash buyer. The state's disclosure form has a line for the school district, and the town's ZIP codes include 14468 for Hilton and 14559 for Spencerport, so a mailing address alone does not tell you which district applies.

sections.h2: Which Greece town rules can slow down a sale?
sections.html:
Open permits and exterior code violations are the two items that most often delay a closing. The Town of Greece Building Department, part of Technical Services at One Vince Tofany Boulevard, requires a permit for remodels and additions to a single-family house, and it requires professionally prepared plans when the work costs more than $20,000.

  • Inspection stages for a permitted job run from footing and foundation through rough framing, insulation, final grading and an electrical sign-off by one of three listed inspection agencies, then a final town inspection.
  • The town's property maintenance law covers vacant land and buildings as well as occupied homes. It sets fines of up to $1,000 or a year in jail per violation, and the town can fix a problem and add the bill to the property tax bill.
  • Every residential property must have active refuse service, and unlicensed or dismantled vehicles may not be stored outdoors.
  • Real estate signs are limited to one sign of six square feet or less, and they cannot go in the right of way or on utility poles.

The permit applications page also lists short-term and long-term rental applications next to the building forms, which matters if the house is a rental you plan to hand over with tenants in place.

sections.h2: How are Greece property taxes billed and collected?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes collects town general taxes in January for the calendar year. The tax collection page says bills are mailed in early January and combine levies for the Town, Monroe County, the Greece Fire District, the Greece Central School District and any special districts. Unpaid school or water bills are re-levied onto this general bill, so ask the closing attorney to check for them.

The town does not set the county, fire district or school rates. It collects on their behalf. You can pay in person at Town Hall on weekdays or use the 24 hour drop at the Service Mall entrance. Online payment goes through the Monroe County website and carries a 3 percent card charge, and the office does not accept payment by phone.

sections.h2: How can a Greece owner contest an assessment before selling?
sections.html:
Greece offers a three step path, and the first step is free and early. The Assessor's page describes it this way.

  • Informal hearing: held from January to March by appointment with the Assessor's Office.
  • Board of Assessment Review: file form RP-524 after May 1 and no later than the fourth Tuesday of May, and ask for a hearing or a paper review.
  • Judicial review: if the board result still looks wrong, form RPTL-730 must be filed with fees within 30 days of final roll publication.

The page says Greece assesses property as of March 1, using the preceding July 1 as the valuation day, and that the office maintains about 34,500 property records and processes roughly 25,000 exemptions. A lower assessment helps a buyer, so a successful challenge before listing can support a better price.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Monroe County?
sections.html:
Greece deeds are filed with the Monroe County Clerk at 39 West Main Street in Rochester. The clerk's land records page lists the current charges, and you must be in line by 4:30 p.m. to record the same day.

  • One page deed: $50, plus $5 for each additional page.
  • TP-584 form: $5.
  • Equalization form RP-5217: $125 for the common residential cases, otherwise $250.
  • Transfer tax: $4 per thousand dollars of price.
  • An added $10 fee applies to each residential deed.

On a $190,000 house the transfer tax line would be $760 and the fixed fees would add roughly $190, so figure about $950 before any attorney charge. Your attorney will confirm the final figure.

sections.h2: What should a Greece seller line up before offers arrive?
sections.html:
• The signed property condition disclosure statement required by Real Property Law section 462, delivered before the buyer signs a binding contract.
  • Permit records for any finished basement, deck, pool or addition.
  • A recent tax bill, so the attorney can see the Town, Monroe County, fire district and school lines.
  • Mortgage payoff information and a list of any liens.
  • Keys, access and a target closing date.

faqs.q: Is Greece, NY part of Rochester?
faqs.a: No. Greece is a separate town in Monroe County, and Rochester is the city on its eastern border. A house in Greece is taxed by the Town of Greece, the county and the fire district, and it is served by Greece Central, Hilton Central or Spencerport Central schools.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit record to sell a Greece house?
faqs.a: The town does not issue a sale permit, but open building permits and exterior code violations can hold up a closing. Ask the Building Department to confirm any past work was closed out.

faqs.q: When do Greece town and county taxes get billed?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed in early January and cover January 1 through December 31. The Receiver of Taxes collects them, and an unpaid school or water bill is moved onto the general tax bill.

faqs.q: How much is the Monroe County transfer tax on a deed?
faqs.a: The clerk lists transfer tax at $4 per thousand dollars of the sale price. A $200,000 sale would carry $800 of that tax, in addition to the recording and form fees.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to grieve a Greece assessment?
faqs.a: Form RP-524 is filed after May 1 and no later than the fourth Tuesday of May. Informal hearings with the Assessor run earlier, from January to March.
